summary: Rabbi Harari explores the significance of the word "Makom" in Parashat Vayesse, where Yaakov discovers God's presence in a place he initially perceived as foreign and distant. The class contrasts this experience with the distant "Makom" of the Akedat Yitzhak, suggesting that one can find spiritual growth and connection to Hashem in their current circumstances rather than always seeking to change their environment. Rabbi Harari encourages listeners to keep their hearts and minds open to finding meaning in their daily lives, even during moments of discomfort or exile.
questions: Why does the Torah repeat the word "Makom" so many times in Parashat Vayesse?
How can we find Hashem in our daily lives when we feel we are not in the right place for growth?
What is the difference between the "Makom" Yaakov found and the "Makom" Avraham traveled to?
Does the concept of "Makom" mean we should stop aspiring to live in Israel?
